reference: GNU coreutils 9.7 shuf and printf (the coreutils shuf and printf verbs).
coverage: Guest compatibility pass 5 (G74/G83): shuf long options, -r/-o/-z and diagnostics; the printf verb behind env printf.
exclusions: shuf output order is random; only counts, sorted members and repeated single values are compared.

cases.purpose: G74: --head-count, --input-range, --echo and prefixes; counts and sorted members are deterministic.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf '%s\n' a b c d e > in; cu shuf --head-count=3 in | wc -l; cu shuf --he 2>/dev/null || true; cu shuf --input-range=1-5 | sort -n; cu shuf --echo x y z | sort; cu shuf -n 0 in; cu shuf --input-range 3-3

cases.purpose: G83: -r draws with replacement (needs -n to stop), -o writes FILE after reading (it may be the input) and -z uses NUL lines.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf '%s
' a b c > in; cu shuf -r -n 6 -e x | tr '
' ' '; echo; cu shuf --repeat --head-count=3 -i 7-7 | tr '
' ' '; echo; cu shuf -o in in; sort -o in in; cat in; printf 'p\0q\0' | cu shuf -z | sort -z | od -c

cases.purpose: G83/G74: GNU shuf's messages and status 1 for bad ranges and counts, conflicting options, extra operands, no lines to repeat and option errors.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; { cu shuf -i 5-3 || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { cu shuf -i 1-2 -i 3-4 || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { cu shuf -n x || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { cu shuf -e -i 1-2 a || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { cu shuf -o a -o b /dev/null || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { cu shuf a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { cu shuf -r </dev/null || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { cu shuf --bogus || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { cu shuf --r </dev/null || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'

cases.purpose: G83: the printf verb (used by env/xargs/nice/nohup printf) is coreutils printf: %q quotes the GNU way, -v is ordinary format text.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; cup() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils printf "$@"; else env printf "$@"; fi; }; cup '%q|%q|%q|%q
' 'a b' "it's" '' 'x$y'; cup '%s-%d
' a 1 b 2; { cup -v x hi || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { cup 'ab%' || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { cup '%s
' a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'

cases.purpose: The printf verb's conversions, flags, widths from arguments, numeric arguments (hex, octal, character constants) and escapes in the format and in %b.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }
cup() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils printf "$@"; else env printf "$@"; fi; }
cup '%5s|%-5s|%.2s|
' ab cd efgh; cup '%c%c|
' hello ''; cup '%d %i %o %x %X %u
' 42 -7 8 255 255 3; cup '%d
' 0x1F 010 "'A" '"b' ' 12' +5
cup '%f %e %g %E %G %a
' 1.5 1e10 0.0001 2 3 1; cup '%.3f|%10.2e|%-8g|
' 3.14159 12345 1e-5; cup '%#o %#x %+d % d %05d
' 8 255 5 5 42
cup '%*d|%-*d|%.*f
' 5 1 4 2 2 3.14159; cup '%*s|%.*s|
' -4 ab -3 abc; cup '%ld %hd %lld %jd %zd %td
' 1 2 3 4 5 6; cup '%%%s
' x
cup '%b|%b|%b
' 'a	b' '\0101\101' '\x41é'; cup '%b%s' 'x\cy' z; echo; cup '\101\0101\8\x41é
'; cup 'a\cb'; echo; cup '%s %d
' a 1 b; cup '%.0s' gone x; echo
cup '%q
' 'a b' "it's" '$x' '' $'tab	here' $'\x01' $'a
b' '~x' 'x=1' '#'; cup '%f %f %g
' inf nan 1e400

cases.purpose: The printf verb's GNU diagnostics: invalid and out-of-range numbers (output continues, status 1), bad directives, missing format, ignored extra arguments.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }
shopt -s extglob
r() { local rc=0 line; "$@" >out 2>err || rc=$?; cat out; while IFS= read -r line; do line=${line#fixture: line +([0-9]): }; printf "%s
" "$line"; done < err; echo "rc=$rc"; }
cup() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils printf "$@"; else env printf "$@"; fi; }
r cup '%d
' abc 1.5 '' 99999999999999999999 -99999999999999999999 08; r cup '%i' 08; r cup '%o' 1e3; r cup '%d' -; r cup '%u
' -1; r cup '%z'; r cup '%'; r cup '%5'; r cup; r cup -x; r cup '%#s' x; r cup '%.5c' x; r cup '%d
' "'"; r cup '%c' '\xff'; r cup '%Lf
' 1.5; r cup '�'; r cup '\u12'; r cup -- '%s
' x; r cup no-directives extra

cases.purpose: shuf --random-source errors, -z/-e/-i interplay, -o write failures and operand checks.
